about: Test vectors for the scoring formula fdbk-score-1 of Agent Reputations (§7, §14). Each vector is the ledger of one (subject, capability) pair of an enrolled subject, evaluated at evaluated_at under the constants below. An event's age runs from the ended_at of the interaction it scores to evaluated_at, in days of 86,400 seconds (§7.2); age_days repeats it for the reader. expect gives a, b, mean, sd, lcb, n_eff and the state, and the pool the events entered with their value v and weight w, in ledger order. An implementation matches a vector when every number is within tolerance of the expected one and the state and the pool's codes are equal. reference.mjs beside this file reproduces every vector.

vectors.name: empty-record
vectors.covers: No events. The pool is empty, the uniform prior alone gives a = b = 1, and n_eff is 0, so the capability is UNPROVEN (§7.4).

vectors.name: thin-record
vectors.covers: Five accepted interactions today. The mean is high and n_eff is 5, so the capability is UNPROVEN and the lower bound shows how little five calls prove (§7.3, §7.4).

vectors.name: just-below-threshold
vectors.covers: Nineteen accepted interactions today, every weight exactly 1. n_eff is 19, below the threshold of 20, so the capability is UNPROVEN (§7.4).

vectors.name: at-threshold
vectors.covers: Twenty accepted interactions today, every weight exactly 1. n_eff is exactly 20, which is not below the threshold, so the capability is RATED (§7.4).

vectors.name: half-life-fading
vectors.covers: Accepted interactions at ages 0, 30, 60, 120 and 365 days. Each weight is 2^(-age/60): 1, 2^-0.5, 0.5, 0.25 and 2^(-365/60). Twenty-four interactions add up to an n_eff below 20, so a record that was RATED when it was fresh has faded to UNPROVEN (§7.2).

vectors.name: ok-corrected
vectors.covers: Ten interactions accepted at once and ten accepted after a correction. OK_CORRECTED contributes 0.6 to a and 0.4 to b (§5).

vectors.name: failed-loudly
vectors.covers: Twenty accepted interactions and four that failed and said so. FAILED contributes 0.15 (§5). Compare failed-silently.

vectors.name: failed-silently
vectors.covers: The same record as failed-loudly, except that the four failures were confident and wrong, found by the caller and attested. FAILED_SILENT contributes 0.0, so the lower bound is lower than in failed-loudly; the gap is the price of honesty (§5). The attestations override the derived outcome OK (§6.3).

vectors.name: declined-and-refused-excluded
vectors.covers: Twenty accepted interactions plus interactions resolved to DECLINED, REFUSED, REFUSED_UNSTATED, UNAVAILABLE and UNREACHABLE. None of those codes enters the pool (§5, §7.1), and an attestation on a DECLINED interaction is rejected because there was no work to judge (§6.2 rule 5). The result equals at-threshold.

vectors.name: value-judgment-reduced-weight
vectors.covers: Twenty accepted interactions and fourteen value judgments on time and materials engagements (ten VALUE_OK, four VALUE_POOR). The engagement facts carry no derived outcome, and each judgment's weight is K_value = 0.5 times its decay weight (§6.6, §7.6), so the fourteen judgments add 7 to n_eff.

vectors.name: publisher-head-start
vectors.covers: A new agent of a publisher whose other agents are RATED for the capability, with a portfolio prior a0 = 9.5, b0 = 2.5 in place of the uniform one: the largest weight §7.5 allows, the equivalent of 10 effective events. Six accepted interactions follow. The prior lifts the mean and the lower bound above thin-record's, and n_eff counts the six direct events only, so the capability stays UNPROVEN: a head start, never an inheritance (§7.5).

vectors.name: nda-breach-not-scored
vectors.covers: Twenty accepted interactions, an upheld breach of an Agent NDA recorded about the subject (nda_resolved with the outcome NDA_BREACH), and an attestation that names NDA_BREACH, which is rejected (§6.2 rule 6). Neither enters the pool (§4.8, §5, §7.1), and the result equals at-threshold.

vectors.name: overrides-amendments-exclusions-probes
vectors.covers: Attestations, amendments, exclusions and probes together. An attestation overrides the derived outcome (§6.3); of two attestations on one interaction only the later scores (§6.2 rule 3); a self-dealing attestation is excluded (§6.4) and the derived outcome stands (§7.1); an attestation with no witnessed interaction is rejected (§6.2 rule 1); probes enter at 1.0 for PASS and 0.0 for FAIL with normal weight (§4.3); a CONTRACT violation contributes 0.0 (§5, §9).
